In twenty twenty-five, a shortage of tiny magnets halted a Ford car factory in Chicago!
Rare-earth magnets sit inside electric motors, cars, drones and wind turbines.
And China makes ninety-four percent of them.
In April twenty twenty-five, it put seven rare earths under licence. In May, its magnet exports fell seventy-four percent in one month.
Within weeks, Ford idled its Chicago plant, and European suppliers shut production lines.
Can the West make its own?
It's trying. The Pentagon bought into a California mine and promised it a minimum price. In Malaysia, Lynas made heavy rare earths outside China for the first time.
But ninety-four percent of the magnets still come from one country.
